styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny stool with a backrest, smaller than one tile, so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged by eye. It uses only 5 distinct colours in total. The nearest same-kind reference, prop-bench-wood, has 14, and the other props have 38-40. The wood shows about 2-3 lightness steps: a light seat, a mid-tone frame and a dark leg and outline tone. The bench shows more steps, with plank highlights, grain and a shaded underside. The candidate has no visible grain, no per-plank highlights and no texture dots. The outline looks like a dark brown-grey that is only slightly tinted, and it wraps most of the shapes. That is closer to the uniform sticker line than to Beodeul's selective dark-material tone, so I rate it mixed. The 0% neutral share of dark edge pixels does speak for a tinted outline, but the piece is still shallower than the reference, thinner and flatter. A careful artist would not accept it next to the bench without adding more shading steps and wood grain.
